item.title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
item.description: Student protesters in France have told the BBC's James Waterhouse that they will continue to take action until change has been made. The protests have now entered their fourth week.

item.title: Inside Katie Zacharia's very brief White House briefing
item.description: The BBC's Sarah Smith was in the room and describes Zacharia's performance and the moment she broke news about Kimberly Guilfoyle being asked to resign.

item.title: Why the lonely in China are hiring 'temporary children'
item.description: A new industry being dubbed the “loneliness economy” has emerged in China, with people hiring themselves out as companions to help the elderly.

item.title: Watch: Witnesses describe 'traumatic' moment man fell out of Six Flags rollercoaster
item.description: One person has died and others were injured after an incident at a US amusement park.

item.title: Watch: Block of flats destroyed in Russian strikes on Ukraine
item.description: BBC Ukraine Correspondent Dan Johnson is in Kyiv, where at least three people were killed in overnight strikes.

item.title: Is Zelensky right to say data centre strikes have taken down Russian bots?
item.description: Experts say there is no evidence that Russian trolls have been affected by Ukraine’s Yandex attacks.

item.title: What we know about the deadly Six Flags rollercoaster incident in Georgia
item.description: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died on Monday after police say he was ejected from a ride at an amusement park.

item.title: Pakistan has locked down Imran Khan's stronghold - but it could backfire
item.description: Some fear the government's standoff with the former PM's supporters could bring more instability, not less.

item.title: Who's to blame for the toxic haze choking South East Asia?

item.description: Police say preliminary information suggests the man who died at the Georgia amusement park fell from a ride.

item.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations

item.description: The Saudi energy ministry says the Houthi attack caused a "limited fire" at Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran.

item.description: The Hokkaido Shimbun journalist is accused of collecting information on Moscow's defence capabilities for Tokyo.

item.title: Lena Dunham's Girls to return for limited HBO run
item.description: Ten years after the series finale, the "Girls" are getting back together to explore the "milestone of turning forty", HBO says.

item.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
item.description: Simbarashe Kundizeza was responding to an accusation that has caused an uproar on social media.

item.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
item.description: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.

item.description: Guilfoyle said the allegations of improper conduct were false and that being ambassador was the "honour of a lifetime".

item.description: It comes ahead of a meeting between the prime minister and President Zelensky at Downing Street.

item.title: World's oldest shipwreck found off coast of Turkey
item.description: Archaeologists say the wreck is up to 4,700 years old, dating to the Early Bronze Age.

item.title: Mauritius reels from worst riots in decades after woman shot by police
item.description: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam imposed a curfew after days of unrest that first began over water shortages.

item.description: It is the latest in a series of crackdowns on media critical of the Turkish president and his government.

item.title: Saudi employee charged with planting recording device in OpenAI office
item.description: Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

item.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
item.description: Four years after the attacks, Serhii Kuznetsov appears in court accused of a plot to destroy Russia's gas pipelines to Germany.

item.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo had a "peaceful night" in the hospital after the surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican says.

item.title: Starlink restrictions affecting Ukraine's front line operations, Kyiv says
item.description: Elon Musk's system allows Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and effectively guide drones to Russian targets.
